About This Data

Energy Burden is the share of a household's total spending that goes toward electricity.

Energy Burden = (Annual Electricity Bill ÷ Total Annual Expenditure) × 100

This is calculated per household, then averaged by parish. A burden above 5% is generally considered high for Jamaica, so it is used as the benchmark when comparing parishes on this map.

Jamaica does not collect direct income data in its national household survey (income is often underreported), so total expenditure is used as the welfare measure instead. This is the standard substitute for income in this kind of analysis.

Averages are unweighted means of household ratios. Households reporting no electricity bill (460 of 1,719) are counted as 0%.

Poverty Rate at the community level is the estimated percentage of a community's population living below Jamaica's poverty line.

It comes from a 2012 small-area statistical model (PIOJ/STATIN), not a direct survey of every community. The national household survey samples too few households to report a reliable figure for each community.

The model combines sparse survey data with the 2011 Population Census. The numbers are modeled estimates: useful for spotting patterns, but with more uncertainty than parish-level survey figures. Select a parish to see its communities colored by poverty rate.

Energy burden (parish level): Jamaica Survey of Living Conditions (JSLC) 2023 microdata. Producer: Statistical Institute of Jamaica (STATIN). Distributed via the Planning Institute of Jamaica (PIOJ) and the SALISES Derek Gordon Databank, UWI Mona. Non-commercial research use.

Poverty rate and consumption (community level): 2012 small-area models, PIOJ/STATIN. Community polygons are simplified for web display.

Grid infrastructure: OpenStreetMap contributors, extracted with Overpass Turbo. Plants are mapped plant polygons plus three wind farms rebuilt from OSM turbine groups. Capacities are as tagged in OSM and several plants have none recorded, so capacity totals are a floor. Coverage may be incomplete in rural parishes.

Parish boundaries: SimpleMaps Jamaica parish boundaries.

Population: Statistical Institute of Jamaica (STATIN), end-of-year 2019 estimate.

Jamaica's Vision 2030 National Development Plan sets long-term goals for economic, social and environmental development, including renewable energy targets and reduced dependence on imported fossil fuels.

The renewable target was raised to 50% of electricity by 2030. Current levels are roughly 10 to 15%.

This tool helps track where energy burden and poverty are concentrated so decarbonization investments can be targeted parish by parish.
